title: Deaths are preventable
article: Three tragic deaths in eight months underline a crying need for more and better facilities and services in Port Hardy.
A week-long inquest into the March 14, 2008 death of 48-year-old Debra Marie Coon found gaps still exist, even though changes were made after the first two deaths.

Port Hardy does not have an adequately equipped observation room where patients who are mentally ill or intoxicated can safely stay. As well as recommending one of those, the latest coroner's jury said there is also a need for trained staff.

The jury was told most people in Port Hardy are blissfully unaware there is an addictions problem, to drugs and alcohol, and recommended that native and non-native local governments work to make people aware of the problems and how to tackle them.
This jury saved the most important message for last, it seems, saying Port Hardy should work on opening a sobering centre, a detoxification centre, a safe house and a treatment centre.
In one way or another, that recommendation was made after all three inquests.
That should be an immediate priority for everyone in Port Hardy and at the senior government levels.
Otherwise the deaths of all three -- Duane Gordon Nelson, Albert William Prevost and Debra Marie Coon -- will have been totally in vain.
